name: Trametes versicolor

tip_speed.note: Veena & Pandey 2012 (Indian J. Agric. Sci. 82:672-675, https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/23047/11181/48969) report 14.93 mm/day at 25 C on malt extract agar, one isolate from the Western Ghats, India. The paper says "linear" growth and does not say radius or diameter; taken here as colony diameter, so halved to 7.47 mm/day radial and x 41.7. If it was radial the value would be 622 um/h. Other reports, also unclear on radius or diameter: 17.4 mm/day at 25 C (Fabros et al. 2023, Studies in Fungi 8:18, Philippine strain)

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Veena & Pandey 2012, Physiological and cultivation requirements of Trametes versicolor, a medicinal mushroom to diversify Indian mushroom industry, Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 82(8):672-675
t_opt.note: malt extract agar, one Indian isolate; rates 8.1, 14.93, 12.73, 12.53 mm/day at 20, 25, 30, 35 C. Reyes et al. 2021 (J. Fungi 7:222) found a Swiss strain fastest at 25 to 30 C; Fabros et al. 2023 found no difference between 25 and 32 C

t_max.source: Veena & Pandey 2012, Physiological and cultivation requirements of Trametes versicolor, a medicinal mushroom to diversify Indian mushroom industry, Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 82(8):672-675
t_max.note: still fast at 35 C (12.53 mm/day), no growth at 40 C; the true limit lies between the two. The same isolate did not grow at 15 C, which is likely a tropical-isolate trait, so t_min is not set from it

cold_drop.source: Veena & Pandey 2012, Physiological and cultivation requirements of Trametes versicolor, a medicinal mushroom to diversify Indian mushroom industry, Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 82(8):672-675
cold_drop.note: fruited on sawdust and rice bran at 24 to 25 C after a spawn run at 25 C, with no cold step; one tropical isolate

size_cm.source: Veena & Pandey 2012, Physiological and cultivation requirements of Trametes versicolor, a medicinal mushroom to diversify Indian mushroom industry, Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 82(8):672-675
size_cm.note: cap width of cultivated fruit bodies, 17 to 100 mm, mean 51 mm, about 1.6 mm thick. First Nature gives up to 10 cm for wild caps (https://www.first-nature.com/fungi/trametes-versicolor.php)

notes: Reported (unchecked) to be the standard test fungus for wood decay and for fungus-against-fungus combat experiments, with a sequenced genome. In beech-block trials it is an early secondary coloniser that deadlocks with Hypholoma fasciculare and is replaced by Phanerochaete velutina (research/06 [4]).
